perineum.title: Before you start: pelvic floor rehabilitation
perineum.text: The pelvic floor is the foundation for everything else. Your **pelvic floor rehabilitation must have started**, with your midwife or a physical therapist trained in pelvic health. Strengthening the abs on a pelvic floor that isn't ready yet can cause or worsen leaks and a feeling of heaviness.

diastasis.title: What is diastasis recti?
diastasis.p1: During pregnancy, the two rectus abdominis muscles move apart to make room for the baby. This is normal. In some women, this gap **persists after giving birth**: a rounded belly, a feeling of abdominal weakness, back pain.
diastasis.p2: At the assessment, I measure your diastasis and assess how your abdominal wall works, so I can adapt the exercises.
diastasis.p3: Surgery is sometimes considered, often as part of a tummy tuck:
diastasis.p3Link: I support you before and after the operation
diastasis.imageAlt: Comparison diagram: on the left, the two rectus abdominis muscles side by side along the linea alba; on the right, a diastasis, with a spindle-shaped gap around the navel, above and below it, while the muscles stay anchored to the ribs at the top and to the pubis at the bottom.
diastasis.caption: The rectus muscles stay anchored to the ribs and the pubis: the gap is around the navel, above and below it.

approach.title: My approach: the whole body
approach.p1: Pregnancy and childbirth change your postural balance: for nine months, your pelvis, back, breathing muscles, rib cage and abs have adapted, as have the muscles in your legs. That's why I offer **whole-body care**, so you can get back to your activities with confidence, as quickly as your body allows.
approach.p2: Elite sport taught me that a comeback is prepared step by step, with clear milestones. Being a mother and an athlete taught me everything else: the tiredness, the lack of time, the wish to get your body back. I bring these two experiences together to support you.

items.question: When can I start?
items.answer: As soon as your pelvic floor rehabilitation has started. The first sessions can take place early in the postpartum period, with gentle work adapted to your recovery. In the hybrid program, the first two sessions take place at the Lyon 5 practice.

items.question: I was on bed rest during my pregnancy. Does that change anything?
items.answer: Yes: after several fairly inactive months, your body has lost strength and endurance, on top of the changes linked to pregnancy. Your return needs to be even more gradual. It's a situation I support often.

items.question: When can I start running again?
items.answer: There is no single date: it depends on your pelvic floor, your abdominal wall, your fitness and your recovery. Together, we set milestones to reach before you start again.

items.question: I've never done any sport. Is this for me?
items.answer: Yes. The postpartum period is a great time to start, with solid foundations and the right support.

items.question: Can I come if I'm breastfeeding?
items.answer: Yes, I adapt the exercises to your tiredness and your pace of life as a new mother.

items.question: Can I have drainage after giving birth?
items.answer: Yes. Alongside your rehabilitation, [Renata França drainage] helps you regain a feeling of lightness in your legs and belly. It's a wellness treatment and is not reimbursed. It is also possible during pregnancy, on prescription, with a legs option adapted to pregnancy.

items.question: Can I do my rehabilitation online?
items.answer: Yes, that's the idea behind both my programs. The hybrid program combines a few sessions at the Lyon 5 practice with online follow-up through the Andrew app and messaging. The 100% online program starts with a video assessment.

items.question: Is it reimbursed?
items.answer: Sessions at the Lyon 5 practice are covered by the French national health insurance and reimbursed on medical prescription. Online follow-up, as a monthly package, is not reimbursed: it is offered with a quote. All prices are given to you before treatment starts.

items.question: Which payment methods do you accept?
items.answer: Cash, cheque, bank transfer and Wero.
